_about: Transcription of the Ohio Euchre Main Quiz (docs/Ohio Euchre answers.pdf) into a machine-readable form. Cards: rank in {9,T,J,Q,K,A} + suit in {C,D,H,S}, e.g. 'JS'=Jack of Spades, 'TD'=Ten of Diamonds. seat: which chair the answerer sits in relative to the dealer (first/second/third/dealer); for play/discard questions, 'S1'/'S2'/'S3'/'partner'/'dealer' in the original text are aliases for the same bidding-order position (1-4, dealer=4). 'turned_down' is set for round-2 (bid2) decisions = the up-card suit rejected in round 1. score is [you, them]. score_dependent flags answers whose correctness hinges on the game score -- observation_tensor has carried a score channel since the match-equity work (see scripts/quiz_eval.py's module docstring), so these are now genuinely evaluated at their stated score, tallied separately from the 'fair' subset rather than excluded as uninformative. stick_the_dealer scenarios depend on the net having been trained with stick_the_dealer=True, true for some checkpoints, not others -- check before trusting a STICK-flagged result. Play-phase questions (build_play_state in scripts/quiz_eval.py) additionally use full_hand/accept/tricks/current_trick/discard fields to reconstruct the exact decision point via real engine replay, asserting narrated trick winners against the engine's own rules.

questions.text: Dealer turned down QC; you called next (spades) and lead JC. S2 plays 9C, S3 plays 9S, dealer plays AS. Lead next?
questions.note: S1-S4 are bidding-order seat aliases (see build_play_state in scripts/quiz_eval.py).
Clubs gives JS(left bower)+AC = 2 strong trump; card-strength call.

questions.text: You bid Diamonds (Next) from first seat; dealer turned down 9H. Lead first?
questions.note: 5th hand card (10C) confirmed by user; missing from the source transcription.
3 diamonds (A-Q-T) + off-ace; card-strength order.
Picking up QD makes Q-T-9 of diamonds; marginal, mild score influence.
Only 2 hearts (A-9) if ordered, and you'd hand dealer the KH; 3 off-aces not enough. Pass.
ZERO trump if clubs ordered -- this is a DONATION at 9-6. Pure score play; model cannot see score.

questions.text: Dealer alone in Hearts. Partner (first seat) leads AS. What do you play?
questions.note: Dealer alone -> dealer's partner (bidding-seat 2) sits out; trick1 leader dealer+1 unaffected since seat2, not seat1, is sitting. up_card unstated by the quiz; arbitrary since PLAY-phase observation never re-exposes it once trump is set.

questions.text: 3rd seat, ordered up KH. Trick1: partner 9C, S2 wins AC, you KC, dealer 9D. S2 leads AS, you trump with Right (JH). Lead next?
questions.note: Trick2's dealer/partner plays (seats 4,1) are unnarrated -- right bower (JH) wins regardless of what they play, so the exact filler cards don't affect the outcome or the decision.

questions.text: Partner orders you to pick up AD (diamonds trump). Discard?

questions.note: 3 hearts (Q-T-9); card-strength call.
3 diamonds A-K-Q + off-ace; strong order.
TRIPLE-INVALID for this net: score-dependent + stick-the-dealer (never trained) + seat not stated in quiz (assumed first). Four jacks = only ever 2 bowers whatever you call.
Spades: AS + JC(left bower) = 2 trump; card-strength call.

questions.text: Partner (3rd seat) orders dealer to pick up 9D (diamonds trump). Lead?

questions.note: Clubs: JC(right)+JS(left) = 2 bowers + 3 off diamonds. The 'alone' is score-driven (9-4, close it out); model can't see score.

questions.text: You (dealer) picked JS (spades trump). S1 leads AD, all follow, you trump with KS. Lead next?
questions.note: hand's already-played KS is included (this entry's transcription uses pre-trick full-hand semantics, unlike most other play questions which show the remaining hand -- options correctly excludes KS, confirming). full_hand is the pre-pickup 5 cards (KS,AH,9H,KC + arbitrary 9C); 9C is explicitly discarded back so the post-pickup hand ends up exactly KS,AH,9H,KC,JS, matching the quiz's given hand.

questions.text: Dealer turns up JC, picking up and going ALONE (clubs trump). Discard?
You are dealer; partner orders up JC (clubs trump). Discard?
2nd seat; 3rd going alone in Hearts. Lead?
questions.note: 3rd (bidding-seat 3) alone -> their partner (bidding-seat 1) sits out, shifting trick1 leadership from seat1 to seat2 (you). Round (self-order vs call) and exact up_card are unstated by the quiz; round1 self-order chosen as the simplest construction that reaches the same PLAY state -- doesn't affect the decision (see build_play_state's docstring).

questions.text: Partner picked up AH (hearts trump). S1 leads TC, you win with your only Ace, S3 follows, partner throws 10S. You hold no trump. Lead back which suit?

questions.note: Picking up JS gives right bower + 9S = 2 trump; marginal, mild score influence.

questions.text: 2nd seat ordered partner (dealer) to pick up 9S (spades trump). S1 leads 9D. What do you play?

questions.note: Spades only K-T (no bower); weak call, likely score/position driven (9-5, partner dealer).

questions.text: Partner (dealer) picked KH (hearts trump). S1 leads TD, you win with Ace, S3 follows. Play next?
questions.note: The winning Ace is inferred as AD (the only card that legally follows TD's diamond lead and is an Ace). Seat3/seat4's unnarrated trick1 plays are filled as non-bower diamonds (JD would be the LEFT BOWER under hearts trump, an effective trump card that would beat the Ace -- caught by the trick-winner assertion), keeping 'you win' true.

JS is the LEFT BOWER under clubs trump (spades/clubs same color) -- only 1 real trump, propped up by weak off-suit help (QD-TD-AD is 3 diamonds but no ace-high strength beyond the ace, QH a lone off-suit queen). Well below the order-up bar; agent wrongly ordered up not-alone.
